title: print() Basics
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how print() puts text on the screen.
learn: print() shows something on the screen
The text goes inside quotes, and the quotes go inside the parentheses
Press Run to see the output
idea: print() is how you make Python show something on the screen. Put your text inside quotes, and put those quotes inside the parentheses. When you press Run, Python follows the instruction and your words show up in the output area. If nothing shows up, check the quotes and parentheses first, because that is where most beginner mistakes happen.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change Hello, world! to Hello, Python! and press Run. The first line of the output should update.

practice.text: Finish the greeting. Keep the first print. Fill in the second blank so it prints a second message.
practice.hint: Keep print("Hello!") as it is. On the blank line, add a second message inside quotes inside print().
practice.starterTip: Under the comment, try: print("Nice to meet you!"). Then press Run.
practice.starter:
print("Hello!")
# Add your second message
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if there are two print() calls that each display a non-empty string.

practice.text: Print your favourite animal in one print() call. Replace the blank.
practice.hint: One print() is enough. Put your animal (or a short sentence about it) inside quotes.
practice.starterTip: Replace the blank with something like: print("panda") or print("I like dogs").
practice.starter:
# One print with your favourite animal
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if one print() shows a non-empty string (animal name or sentence). Empty print() fails.

quiz.question: What does print("Hello!") do?

options.text: It saves Hello! forever in a file
It displays Hello! on the screen
It creates a variable named Hello

quiz.correct: Right, print() shows the text on the screen.
quiz.wrong: Not this one. print() only displays text, it does not create a variable or save anything.

quiz.question: Which line is written correctly?
quiz.correct: Yes, you need a lowercase print, parentheses, and quotes around the text.
quiz.wrong: Check both parts. The text needs quotes, and print has to be lowercase with parentheses.

quiz.question: Why do we put quotes around Hello in print("Hello")?

options.text: So Python knows it is text to show
Quotes make the program run faster
Quotes turn print into a comment

quiz.correct: Quotes mark a string. Text for Python to print.
quiz.wrong: Quotes tell Python the words are text, not a variable name.
